movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (Total Group)', column FY25 -> column FY26
headline: CBA Group net interest margin fell 3 bps in FY26, from 2.08% (208 bps) in FY25 to 2.05% (205 bps), on the bank's primary reporting basis per the results book's Total Group NIM row (ev-5, ev-14, ev-15). Lower lending margins (asset pricing -5 bps), liquid-asset and repo drag (-3 bps) and Treasury & Markets (-2 bps) drove the decline, partly offset by replicating portfolio and capital hedge earnings (+5 bps) and favourable mix (+2 bps); funding costs and basis risk were flat at 0 bps. Excluding liquids and pooled facilities, margins were broadly stable (underlying NIM 2.04% to 2.05%, ev-13).

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year -> Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Book walk shows Liquids at -3 bps; the slide shows -4 bps as Liquids & repos (ev-4). Drag from +$15bn average liquid assets and +$11bn average institutional repos (ev-18), which the bank calls broadly neutral to net interest income (ev-7).

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year -> Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Lending margins fell 5 bps, the largest single drag, identical in both the book and slide walks (ev-1, ev-4) and consistent with the bank's commentary on lower lending margins (ev-7).

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year -> Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Funding costs flat FY-on-FY at 0 bps in both walks (ev-1, ev-4). The Dec 2025 -> Jun 2026 half-on-half walk shows +2 bps (ev-2, ev-3), so funding pressure emerged only in 2H26. No deposit-versus-wholesale split disclosed.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year -> Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Favourable portfolio mix added 2 bps in both walks (ev-1, ev-4), reflecting the mix benefit of growth in business lending and deposits cited in the results narrative (ev-7).

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year -> Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Basis risk (bills/OIS spread) contributed 0 bps FY-on-FY per the book's walk (ev-1). The slide's FY walk omits this bar, so the published zero is single-source.

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year -> Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Largest positive at +5 bps from capital, replicating portfolio and hedge earnings (ev-1); the slide shows the same +5 bps labelled Interest rate risk hedging (ev-4). Narrative cites higher earnings on replicating portfolio and capital hedges (ev-7).

drivers.columns: Jun 25 Full Year -> Jun 26 Full Year
drivers.narrative: Treasury & Markets subtracted 2 bps per the book's walk (ev-1); the slide shows -1 bps, allocating 1 bp of drag to Liquids & repos instead (ev-4). Definitional split; both walks total -3 bps.

notable_items: No notable items are flagged on the Group NIM row or within the FY25 -> FY26 margin walk.
Underlying NIM excluding liquids and pooled facilities rose 1 bp, 2.04% to 2.05% (ev-13) - a named variant, context only.
Average liquid assets rose +$15bn and average institutional repos +$11bn in FY26 vs FY25 (ev-18).

disagreements.topic: Liquids drag in the FY25 -> FY26 walk
values: -4 bps - results presentation walk, Liquids & repos (ev-4)
disagreements.preferred: -3 bps from the profit announcement walk (ev-1)
disagreements.explanation: The slide folds institutional repos into its Liquids & repos bar while the book's walk separates them; the 1 bp difference mirrors the Treasury & Markets difference. Both walks sum to -3 bps. Book framing adopted per the source hierarchy.

disagreements.topic: Treasury & Markets in the FY25 -> FY26 walk
disagreements.explanation: Mirror of the liquids allocation difference: the slide moves 1 bp of drag from Treasury & Markets into Liquids & repos. Totals unchanged at -3 bps.

disagreements.topic: Headline Group NIM vs underlying NIM variant
values: 2.08% -> 2.05% (-3 bps) - profit announcement Group NIM (ev-5, ev-14)
disagreements.preferred: Headline Group NIM from the profit announcement
disagreements.explanation: Underlying NIM is a named variant excluding liquids and pooled facilities; it cannot supply the Group movement. Context: on that basis margins improved about 1 bp, consistent with the bank's broadly-stable ex-liquids commentary (ev-7).

disagreements.topic: Group margin levels on presentation p60 table
values: FY25 208 / FY26 205 - same-page walk (ev-4) and profit announcement (ev-5, ev-14)
disagreements.explanation: ev-16's period labels appear swapped relative to the same page's walk chart and the results book; the swap was disregarded and the movement taken from the profit announcement.

limitations: Results-book NIM table column headers are not verbatim in the evidence; FY25 and FY26 were inferred from the table quotes (ev-5, ev-13, ev-14).
Walk bar values are vision-extracted from charts (ev-1, ev-4) at whole-bps precision; no finer granularity is available.
The single Funding costs bar is not split between deposits and wholesale, so funding.deposits and funding.wholesale cannot be quantified separately.
Basis risk 0 bps appears only in the book's walk (ev-1); the slide walk omits the bar.
ev-16's FY26/FY25 labels appear swapped versus every corroborating record; treated as an extraction error and excluded.
Divisional margin rows (ev-8 to ev-12) are single-segment measures and were excluded from the Group movement.

evidence_records.quote: [walk chart] NIM Movement since June 2025: Jun 25 Full Year 208 -> Jun 26 Full Year 205
[walk chart] NIM Movement since December 2025: Dec 25 Half 204 -> Jun 26 Half 206
[walk chart] Group margin – 12 months: FY25 208.0 -> FY26 205.0

Margins were broadly stable excluding growth in liquid assets and institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income. Underlying margins were supported by higher earnings on replicating portfolio and capital hedges, and the favourable mix impact of growth in business lending and deposits, largely offset by lower lending margins.
